_comment: T2 — single source of truth for the CI e2e synthetic fixtures.
Consumed by scripts/ci/seed-e2e.mjs (writes them) and tests/e2e/helpers/auth.ts (logs in as them),
so a credential can never drift between the seeder and the specs.
SYNTHETIC ONLY (Ley 21.719): example.com is RFC 2606 reserved, the names are invented,
and these credentials are only ever valid on the ephemeral local Supabase stack the CI job
starts and destroys. The seeder refuses to run against a non-local Supabase URL.
Z1c — extended with the personas the Zoom join-authz matrix needs; QA-ROLES completed the
roster so that all nine roles in types/roles.ts have a synthetic account.
SCOPE FIELDS — the five optional fields that place a persona in the organization, plus
`inactiveRoles`. WHERE THEY LAND DEPENDS ON WHERE THEY ARE WRITTEN:
TOP LEVEL, on a persona   `school` and `generation` set the PROFILE scope
(profiles.school_id / profiles.generation_id) AND the
PRIMARY role row's scope. `roleScope`, `community` and
`network` are role-row concepts and touch the primary role
row only — a profile has no such columns.
INSIDE inactiveRoles      every field affects THAT INACTIVE ROLE ROW AND NOTHING ELSE.
An inactiveRoles entry NEVER writes to profiles: the profile
is written once per persona, in pass 1, from the top-level
fields alone. An entry with `school: secondary` produces a
deactivated role row at the secondary school while the
persona's profile stays where its top-level `school` put it.
The five scope fields, and the ONLY values each accepts (absent is always allowed;
anything else THROWS — scripts/ci/e2e-fixture-scopes.mjs, which is the enforced copy of
this list):
school        'primary' (default) | 'secondary'. Names a top-level school block
(`school` / `schoolSecondary`). At the top level it sets BOTH
profiles.school_id and the primary role row's user_roles.school_id;
inside inactiveRoles it sets only that row's user_roles.school_id.
`directivo` and `directivoSecondary` are the two equipo_directivo
personas this field separates. The one scope field whose absence is not
'no scope' — absent means the primary school.
roleScope     'global' — user_roles.school_id is NULL, overriding `school` for the role
row it is written on. ROLE ROWS ONLY: a profile is never global, so a
top-level `roleScope` leaves profiles.school_id at whatever `school`
said. Only consultor reads this distinction
(lib/utils/session-policy.ts:31 treats consultor.school_id IS NULL as
GLOBAL). Absent means the role row takes `school`.
generation    'primary' — names the top-level `generation` block. At the top level it
sets BOTH profiles.generation_id and the primary role row's
user_roles.generation_id; inside inactiveRoles it sets only that row's
user_roles.generation_id. Carried only by lider_generacion:
user_roles.generation_id is reserved for that role and every other
persona leaves it NULL. Absent means NULL.
community     'zoom' -> zoom.community.id | 'role' -> roleCommunity.id. ROLE ROWS ONLY
(user_roles.community_id). The two communities are distinct on purpose:
`communityManager` holds a REAL community scope that is NOT the Zoom
session's, so its denial in the authz matrix is a WRONG-scope denial
rather than a no-scope one. Absent means NULL.
network       'primary' -> network.id | 'secondary' -> networkSecondary.id. ROLE ROWS
ONLY (user_roles.red_id). See NETWORK TOPOLOGY below. Absent means NULL.
inactiveRoles extra role rows seeded with is_active=false, to prove deactivation denies.
Each entry takes its own `role` plus the same five scope fields, scoped to
that row alone as described above.
FAIL-CLOSED. An unsupported value — 'primry', 'seconday', 'Global' — is rejected before
the seeder builds a client, naming the persona, the field and the accepted values. It used
to fall through to the primary fixture or to NULL, which seeded a scope nobody asked for
and made every spec that trusted it pass for the wrong reason. Adding a value means
editing SCOPE_VALUES in scripts/ci/e2e-fixture-scopes.mjs and this list together;
__tests__/scripts/ci/e2e-fixture-scopes.test.ts holds them to it.
NETWORK TOPOLOGY — two synthetic networks, disjoint by construction:
network           'Red Sintetica E2E'        holds school `primary`    supervised by networkSupervisor
networkSecondary  'Red Sintetica E2E Norte'  holds school `secondary`  supervised by NOBODY
`networkSupervisor` is assigned to the primary network ONLY. `networkSecondary` is a fully
seeded network — real row, real school link — that no persona in the roster holds any role
in. That is the reusable CROSS-NETWORK NEGATIVE CONTROL: a later batch asserting a
supervisor_de_red denial can point at a populated network its supervisor genuinely does not
supervise, rather than at an empty or non-existent id, which would pass for the wrong reason.
LIMITATION — tests/e2e/ci-fixture.spec.ts proves the TOPOLOGY and only the topology: which
network each persona's role row carries, and which school each network holds, read back
through the product's own admin API. It does NOT prove that any product surface denies
cross-network access. Each affected batch must add its own product-level denial test.
The `zoom` block is the domain graph seeded by scripts/ci/seed-e2e-zoom.mjs. Its ids are fixed
so the seeding is idempotent and the specs can address the rows without a lookup.
Z1c-2 — two sessions, because one cannot exercise both branches of the disclosure rule:
session        meeting_link NULL — the provisionable-but-unprovisioned case, and the
`meet-no-link` branch of the interstitial.
linkedSession  a legacy MANUAL meeting link — the case Z1a's interstitial was built for.
It is the session that can prove stripping: a non-privileged caller must
get has_meeting/join_path and NOT the raw link. It carries the attendees
and the two report visibilities too, so one GET exercises all three tier-2
assertions (no e-mail, no raw link, no facilitators_only report) at once.
The link host is example.net — RFC 2606 reserved, like the addresses. No real meeting.
Z2-S8 (r28) — a THIRD session, added because both of the above are unmanaged:
managedSession is_zoom_managed true — the case this whole phase exists to serve, and
the one no e2e had ever exercised. `is_zoom_managed` is NOT NULL DEFAULT
false and the seeder never wrote it, so every seeded session was
unmanaged and the managed branches of the interstitial, of the .ics
endpoints and of the disclosure layer had only ever run in unit tests.
ADDED, NEVER FLIPPED. `session` and `linkedSession` keep is_zoom_managed false, so
every assertion already written against them holds unchanged. A managed session carries
NO meetingLink by design (plan §8: the join URL lives in zoom_internal and never touches
consultor_sessions) — that is the property under test, not a gap in the fixture.
A8 — `pasantiasLead` is one row of public.pasantias_leads for the admin triage surface.
It is a TOP-LEVEL block on purpose: a key under `users` would break
assertFixtureRosterComplete() in tests/e2e/helpers/auth.ts, which requires `users` and
DECLARED_FIXTURE_KEYS to be set-equal. The specs only ever READ it — the fixture is not
reset between local runs, so a spec that triaged it would pass once and fail forever after.
PASANT-B004 (C009) — `pasantiasBulk` describes 1205 OWNED synthetic contacts for the admin
leads surface at scale (PostgREST max_rows = 1000). 1205 is the BULK count only: the table
also holds the A8 lead above and every contact the journey specs submit, so no spec may
read 1205 as the table total. Bulk-only expectations are scoped by `searchToken`, which only
the owned e-mails carry. Every bulk created_at is before 2026-07-01, i.e. older than any A8
lead (the table dates from 2026-07-31), so the A8 lead's place among the newest 50 — which
tests/e2e/pasantias-leads-admin.spec.ts relies on — is unchanged. Ownership is the fixed id
namespace `idPrefix`: the seeder writes those ids and nothing else, never deletes, never
touches the A8 lead. `expected` is written out by hand; the seeder refuses to write if its
generated rows disagree with it, and the specs compare the live API with it.
PASANT-B004 — `users.adminForcedPassword` is the one persona seeded with
must_change_password = true (`mustChangePassword`). Every other persona has no such field
and is seeded false, exactly as before. It is a real global admin held by the forced
password gate: its login lands on /change-password, and the specs prove the PASANT admin
API refuses it. Nothing may submit its change-password form — that would clear the flag.

_comment: Contact NNNN (index 1..count, four digits) has id idPrefix + NNNN padded to 12 digits,
e-mail emailPrefix + NNNN + '@' + emailDomain, first name firstName, last name
lastNamePrefix + NNNN and institution `institution`. Decimal digits are valid hex, so id
order is index order.
kind = kinds[(index - 1) mod 5]; status = statuses[floor((index - 1) / 5) mod 4].
Cohort is cohorts.historical for kind `historical` and cohorts.january otherwise; kinds
`historical` and `unclassified` have no interest row, `both` has inspira and
mirada-profunda, the single kinds have that one program.
created_at comes from the run holding the index: createdAt, plus (to - index)
microseconds when ladderMicros is true. consent_accepted_at and each interest's
created_at / consent_accepted_at equal the contact's created_at.
`hostile` overrides text columns of named contacts and never their identity, kind,
status, timestamps, e-mail or last name; `csv` is the cell the downloaded CSV must hold,
worked out by hand from lib/exportUtils.ts (formula prefix ', CR/CRLF -> LF, RFC 4180).
`expected` is hand-computed, never generated. The seeder checks its rows against it.
